3  	description: API Reference for the cookies function.
4  	---
5  	
6  	`cookies` is an **async** function that allows you to read the HTTP incoming request cookies in [Server Components](/docs/app/getting-started/server-and-client-components), and read/write outgoing request cookies in [Server Functions](/docs/app/getting-started/mutating-data) or [Route Handlers](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route).
7  	
8  	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
9  	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
10 	
11 	export default async function Page() {
12 	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
13 	  const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
14 	  return '...'
15 	}
16 	```
17 	
18 	```js filename="app/page.js" switcher
19 	import { cookies } from 'next/headers'
20 	
21 	export default async function Page() {
22 	  const cookieStore = await cookies()
23 	  const theme = cookieStore.get('theme')
24 	  return '...'
25 	}
26 	```
27 	
28 	## Reference
29 	
30 	### Methods
31 	
32 	The following methods are available:
33 	
34 	| Method                      | Return Type      | Description                                                                     |
35 	| --------------------------- | ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
36 	| `get('name')`               | Object           | Accepts a cookie name and returns an object with the name and value.            |
37 	| `getAll()`                  | Array of objects | Returns a list of all the cookies with a matching name.                         |
38 	| `has('name')`               | Boolean          | Accepts a cookie name and returns a boolean based on if the cookie exists.      |
39 	| `set(name, value, options)` | -                | Accepts a cookie name, value, and options and sets the outgoing request cookie. |
40 	| `delete(name)`              | -                | Accepts a cookie name and deletes the cookie.                                   |
41 	| `toString()`                | String           | Returns a string representation of the cookies.                                 |
42 	
43 	### Options
44 	
45 	When setting a cookie, the following properties from the `options` object are supported:
46 	
47 	| Option        | Type                                   | Description                                                                        |
48 	| ------------- | -------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
49 	| `name`        | String                                 | Specifies the name of the cookie.                                                  |
50 	| `value`       | String                                 | Specifies the value to be stored in the cookie.                                    |
51 	| `expires`     | Date                                   | Defines the exact date when the cookie will expire.                                |
52 	| `maxAge`      | Number                                 | Sets the cookie’s lifespan in seconds.                                             |
53 	| `domain`      | String                                 | Specifies the domain where the cookie is available.                                |
54 	| `path`        | String, default: `'/'`                 | Limits the cookie's scope to a specific path within the domain.                    |
55 	| `secure`      | Boolean                                | Ensures the cookie is sent only over HTTPS connections for added security.         |
56 	| `httpOnly`    | Boolean                                | Restricts the cookie to HTTP requests, preventing client-side access.              |
57 	| `sameSite`    | Boolean, `'lax'`, `'strict'`, `'none'` | Controls the cookie's cross-site request behavior.                                 |
58 	| `priority`    | String (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`) | Specifies the cookie's pri

14 	> This page covers caching with [Cache Components](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents), enabled by setting [`cacheComponents: true`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.ts` file. If you're not using Cache Components, see the [Caching and Revalidating (Previous Model)](/docs/app/guides/caching-without-cache-components) guide.
15 	
16 	Caching is a technique for storing the result of data fetching and other computations so that future requests for the same data can be served faster, without doing the work again.
17 	
18 	## Enabling Cache Components
19 	
20 	You can enable Cache Components by adding the [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) option to your Next config file:
21 	
22 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher
23 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
24 	
25 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
26 	  cacheComponents: true,
27 	}
28 	
29 	export default nextConfig
30 	```
31 	
32 	```js filename="next.config.js" switcher
33 	/** @type {import('next').NextConfig} */
34 	const nextConfig = {
35 	  cacheComponents: true,
36 	}
37 	
38 	module.exports = nextConfig
39 	```
40 	
41 	> **Good to know:** When Cache Components is enabled, `GET` Route Handlers follow the same prerendering model as pages. See [Route Handlers with Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/route-handlers#with-cache-components) for details.
42 	
43 	## Usage
44 	
45 	The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels:
46 	
47 	- **Data-level**: Cache a function that fetches or computes data (e.g., `getProducts()`, `getUser(id)`)
48 	- **UI-level**: Cache an entire component or page (e.g., `async function BlogPosts()`)
49 	
50 	A cache directive gives a result a lifetime, which Next.js uses for time-based revalidation and rendering optimizations. For on-demand revalidation after a mutation, see [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). See [Prerendering](#prerendering) for how cached results become part of the static shell and may be included in a [prefetch](#prefetching).
51 	
52 	> **Good to know:** We recommend pairing every cache directive with a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). Without one, the implicit `default` profile applies.
53 	
54 	Arguments and any values captured from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries. See [cache output](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-output) for what an entry holds, and [serialization requirements and constraints](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#constraints) for details on what can be cached and how arguments work.
55 	
56 	### Data-level caching
57 	
58 	To cache an asynchronous function that fetches data, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the function body:
59 	
60 	```tsx filename="app/lib/data.ts" highlight={1,4,5}
61 	import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache'
62 	
63 	export async function getUsers() {
64 	  'use cache'
65 	  cacheLife('hours')
66 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM users')
67 	}
68 	```
69 	
70 	Data-level caching is useful when the same data is used across multiple components, or when you want to cache the data independently from the UI.

43 	## Usage
44 	
45 	The [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive caches the return value of async functions and components. You can apply it at two levels:

50 	A cache directive gives a result a lifetime, which Next.js uses for time-based revalidation and rendering optimizations. For on-demand revalidation after a mutation, see [Revalidating](/docs/app/getting-started/revalidating). See [Prerendering](#prerendering) for how cached results become part of the static shell and may be included in a [prefetch](#prefetching).
51 	
52 	> **Good to know:** We recommend pairing every cache directive with a [`cacheLife`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cacheLife). Without one, the implicit `default` profile applies.
53 	
54 	Arguments and any values captured from parent scopes automatically become part of the [cache key](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-keys), which means different inputs will produce separate cache entries. See [cache output](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#cache-output) for what an entry holds, and [serialization requirements and constraints](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache#constraints) for details on what can be cached and how arguments work.

57 	
58 	To cache an asynchronous function that fetches data, add the `use cache` directive at the top of the function body:

62 	
63 	export async function getUsers() {
64 	  'use cache'
65 	  cacheLife('hours')
66 	  return db.query('SELECT * FROM users')
67 	}
68 	```
69 	
70 	Data-level caching is useful when the same data is used across multiple components, or when you want to cache the data independently from the UI.
